The 2011-12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team had a historic season, achieving several program milestones:

## Key Achievements
- **Record**: 26-5 overall, 12-2 in Ivy League play
- **NCAA Tournament**: Made their first NCAA Tournament appearance since 1946
- **Ivy League Champions**: Won the Ivy League title

## Coaching and Leadership
- **Head Coach**: Tommy Amaker (5th season)
- **Key Players**: 
  - Kyle Casey (forward/center)
  - Keith Wright (senior forward) - Ivy League Player of the Year
  - Oliver McNally
  - Brandyn Curry (guard)
  - Christian Webster

## Season Highlights
- Started the season 10-0, the best start in program history
- Won the Ivy League championship outright
- Earned a 12-seed in the NCAA Tournament
- Faced 5-seed Vanderbilt in the first round of the NCAA Tournament (lost 79-70)
- The team's 26 wins were a program record at the time

## Significance
This season marked a turning point for Harvard basketball:
- Ended a 66-year NCAA Tournament drought
- Established Harvard as a legitimate basketball program
- Part of Tommy Amaker's transformation of Harvard basketball from perennial Ivy League doormat to championship contender

The 2011-12 season laid the foundation for Harvard's continued success, including subsequent NCAA Tournament appearances and upset victories in following years.
